clue.text: Much-visited place indicated by mark on dial?

definitions.meaning: a scenic spot that tourists flock to see
dial is slang for face, so this is a small dark mole on the cheek, once thought attractive

explanation.surface: A hint that a famous tourist site is marked by a symbol on some instrument's face.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are fixed phrases: a scenic landmark and a cosmetic mole on the face, 'dial' being slang for face.

clue.text: Snapper with pornographic angle?

parts.note: a blue film is a pornographic one
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A photographer with a smutty take on things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapper' looks like a photographer, but it is a fish; the bluefish is also known as a snapper.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluefish is a fierce sea fish whose young are called snappers in America.

clue.text: Article taken from national about one living off the workers?

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the remaining letters are shuffled
the article is removed from the word national before the rest is rearranged

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A political jibe about a parasite who lives off the labour of the working class.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one A out of NATIONAL and the 'about' anagram turns NTIONAL into the answer. 'Workers' are worker ants, the larva's prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The larva of this insect sits in a sand pit and preys on ants, the archetypal worker insects.

clue.text: According to paper, Europeans finding means to sustain simultaneous conversations?

parts.note: the Telegraph is a British daily newspaper
Poles are natives of Poland

explanation.surface: A newspaper report that some Europeans have found a way of keeping several conversations going at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is whimsical: the posts hold up the wires that carried many calls at once.
explanation.definitionFit: These wooden posts carry the overhead wires along which many telephone calls travel at the same time.

clue.text: Car user, MP, involved in

annotationWithheld.why: Car user, MP, involved in (9): USER+MP+IN gives only eight of the nine letters, one I is missing, so the clue as held looks cut short

clue.text: Like Humpty Dumpty, poet has nothing to eat

indicators.note: the poet takes the nothing inside him as if swallowing it

parts.note: Ovid was the Roman poet of the Metamorphoses
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme comparison: the poet is going hungry, like the egg-shaped figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Humpty Dumpty is drawn as an egg, and the word means egg-shaped.

clue.text: Paid for meal

definitions.meaning: ..., informally given a fee for work
a ..., as for a baby or animal

explanation.surface: Someone settled the bill for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A person given a fee has been fee'd, and a feed is a serving of food, as for a baby.

clue.text: Those permanently leaving country before catching plane start to sob

indicators.note: the word for before closes round the plane, catching it inside

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a MiG is a Russian fighter plane

indicators.note: only the first letter of sob is taken

explanation.surface: Emigrants about to leave home begin sobbing as they board a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay; 'before' is ERE, not a signal for order.
explanation.definitionFit: Exiles who have left their homeland for good, typically for political reasons.

clue.text: Squirrel household plays host to American relaxing

indicators.note: the nest takes in the abbreviation as a guest, holding it inside

parts.note: a drey is a squirrel's nest

explanation.surface: A family of squirrels entertains an easygoing visitor from the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soothing and gentle, like a reverie, is calm and restful.

clue.text: Issue dealt with in class

parts.note: issue means offspring, and the young people taught in classrooms are the issue in question

explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a topic discussed in a lesson; here it means offspring, young people who are taught in class.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils are young offspring who receive lessons together in a classroom.

clue.text: Not after characters participating in hunt illegally?

indicators.note: the letters that take part in the words hunt illegally contain the answer

explanation.surface: A question about letters taking part in poaching.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Not after' means up to the time of, as in 'wait up to six'.

clue.text: Ban for professional writer

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a scribe is one who writes

explanation.surface: Barring an expert author from doing something.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbid or outlaw something officially.

clue.text: Both ends of drain blocked in Leicester?

indicators.note: points at the first and last letters of the drain word
those outer letters are stopped off, so they are removed

parts.note: a sewer is a drain for waste

explanation.surface: A plumbing problem in a Midlands city: a drain stopped up at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicester is the English city, but also a breed of sheep, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leicester is a long-wool breed of sheep, and a female of it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Heather's after a fellow for a casual affair

indicators.note: heather is placed after the fellow

parts.note: ling is another name for heather; the 's means is

explanation.surface: Heather is chasing a man for a no-strings romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A short romantic or sexual relationship with no commitment.

clue.text: System of grooves and channels producing sound?

definitions.text: System of grooves and channels producing sound?

parts.words: System of grooves and channels producing sound?
parts.note: a single cabinet with record grooves to play and radio channels to tune, both making sound

explanation.walkthrough: Reads like plumbing or irrigation; the grooves are on records and the channels are radio stations.
explanation.definitionFit: A combined record player and wireless set in one cabinet.

clue.text: Some annalist is becoming involved in lurid distortions of stories

indicators.note: the letters become tangled up together into a new order

explanation.surface: A chronicler gets caught up in lurid misreporting.
explanation.definitionFit: Presenting news in a shocking, exaggerated way to excite readers.

clue.text: The jail squares on Monopoly boards?

definitions.text: The jail squares on Monopoly boards?

parts.words: The jail squares on Monopoly boards?
parts.note: on the board game Monopoly the jail corner is where a player is not able to pass the Go square

explanation.walkthrough: In Monopoly a player sent to jail may not pass Go, so the jail corner is a place where you cannot 'go': the pun on the Go square.
explanation.definitionFit: Places that are dangerous or forbidden to enter; jailed Monopoly players cannot pass Go.

clue.text: Agonisingly keen about love, something that burns

indicators.note: the rearranged keen goes about, around, the love god
agonisingly suggests writhing, so the letters of keen are twisted into a new order

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: Someone painfully eager in romance, compared to a burning flame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agonisingly' turns KEEN into KENE, which goes 'about' EROS: K + EROS + ENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin oil, a fuel burnt in lamps and heaters.

clue.text: Battling against the odds?

parts.note: battling is fighting and odds are a chance, so this is a slim but real prospect of success

explanation.walkthrough: Reads as struggling against heavy odds; split it as fighting (battling) plus chance (odds).
explanation.definitionFit: A possibility of success if great effort is made.

clue.text: Endlessly sardonic about encroachments

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened word is rearranged
the word sardonic loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone forever mocking the gradual invasion of territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts the C from SARDONIC and 'about' rearranges SARDONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Advances into someone else's territory, gradually eating away at it.

clue.text: Greyish-yellow sort of bread, sharp-tasting

parts.note: naan is an Indian flatbread, often spelt nan
keen can mean pungent or acute in flavour

explanation.surface: A description of a pale, tangy loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a yellowish cotton cloth from Nanjing came to be used for its buff colour.

clue.text: Youngster almost cut by edges of schoolmate's tool

indicators.note: the shortened youngster is cut open by letters going inside it
the last letter of the youngster word is dropped

parts.note: a child is a youngster

indicators.note: the first and last letters of schoolmate are taken

explanation.surface: A child gets nicked by a classmate's implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the D from CHILD; 'edges of' takes S and E from schoolmate.
explanation.definitionFit: A bladed hand implement for cutting wood or stone.

clue.text: Wind instrument, one a monarch played

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are performed in a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A king plays a mouth organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth organ, a small instrument blown through reeds.

clue.text: Insect, one landing on giant, tailless

indicators.note: in a down answer the one sits on top of the giant

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the giant loses its last letter

parts.note: Magog is a legendary giant, of Gog and Magog

explanation.surface: An insect alights on a huge figure that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The final adult stage of an insect after metamorphosis.

clue.text: A common language

parts.note: common in the sense of vulgar or informal, so slang or jargon, as well as a shared tongue

explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' reads as shared; it also means low or informal, the sense of this word for jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal speech or jargon, especially foreign or specialist talk.

clue.text: Left-winger about to go to Germany

parts.note: re means about or concerning
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A socialist about to head for Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a communist or socialist, from the colour of the revolutionary flag.

clue.text: Computer programs for ploughmen?

parts.note: a ploughshare is the blade of a plough, so cutting-blade goods would suit farmers

explanation.walkthrough: A share is a plough blade, so the pun reads the software as goods (wares) of shares, suited to ploughmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Software distributed free on trial, with payment requested for continued use.

clue.text: Female flier about to meet first lady

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A woman pilot is about to meet the President's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female flier' sounds like an aviator; it is a bird, the female ruff.
explanation.definitionFit: The female of the ruff, a wading bird, has its own name.

clue.text: Inventory is kept by junior officer

indicators.note: the officer holds the word is inside

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A lieutenant keeps the stock list.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue or itemised record of goods.

clue.text: Agreement reached by canons once in disarray?

indicators.note: disarray means disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Squabbling clergy finally come to terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmony or accord between things or people.
